result.title: PIAE: Physics-Informed Continuous Autoencoding for Compact 3D Human Motion
result.summary: Temporal compression reduces the sequence length that motion generators must model, but can damage articulated detail and global trajectory. These errors have unequal consequences: root-velocity and heading errors propagate through trajectory recovery and affect the placement of the entire body. We propose PIAE, a physics-informed continuous autoencoder that allocates a fixed token budget between explicitly retained kinematic signals and complementary learned features. At 8 x temporal compression, each 256-dimensional token contains 224 learned values and a 32-dimensional physical carrier. The complete token conditions neural decoding, while a parallel recovery path constrains selected outputs. On the official HumanML3D benchmark, PIAE achieves 8.936 mm global MPJPE, an 82.0% reduction relative to a same-width learned-only model. The benefit extends beyond trajectory restoration: facing-local neural-body error before analytical correction decreases by 76.6% in a frozen-checkpoint validation diagnostic, and supplying the same true trajectory to both models preserves the body-quality advantage. Targeted root-only and explicit-root hybrid controls establish strong trajectory-aware comparisons; alternative carriers reveal that torso references favor position accuracy, whereas stance anchors favor support quality. With the original 8 x AEs frozen, matched text-to-motion generators predict every carrier value and improve FID from 0.506 to 0.163. Frozen reconstruction also transfers to AIST++ without adaptation. The compressed carrier interface reduces measured generation time by 27.8% relative to its 1 x counterpart. Together, these findings demonstrate that selective preservation can use a fixed representation budget more effectively, improving neural articulated reconstruction and downstream generation in compact human motion.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PIAE，一种物理信息连续自编码器，在固定 token 预算下把 latent 划分为显式保留的运动学载体与学习特征，并用并行恢复路径约束解码，用于紧凑 3D 人体运动的压缩与下游生成。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「固定预算内显式载体＋学习特征」的划分与受约束恢复路径，可能为 LVR 中如何在 latent 状态里保留任务必要信息、抑制信息坍缩提供可供核查的借鉴；但任务为人体运动压缩而非视觉推理，需人工判断可迁移性。
